Description: The official Indian Standard designator, including part/section and year.
Notes: Primary key. Keep the exact BIS formatting (spaces, colon, parentheses for parts).

Description: Official title of the standard as published by BIS, including revision label.
Example: Plain and Reinforced Concrete — Code of Practice (Fourth Revision)
Notes: Titles can be long; do not truncate for storage, only for UI display.

Description: A short scope/description of what the standard covers, drawn from its published scope clause.
Example: Covers general structural use of plain and reinforced concrete...
Always Available?: No — many standards' full scope was not retrieved in this pass
Can We Store It?: Yes (short paraphrase only, not full clause text)
Notes: Full scope clauses are BIS copyrighted text — store only a short paraphrase, never the verbatim clause. See File 03 (copyright note).

Description: High-level procurement category (see File 04 taxonomy).
Source: Assigned by team, not by BIS
Notes: This is our own categorisation layer, not an official BIS field.

Description: Broader procurement sector, useful for filtering across multiple categories.
Notes: Coarser grouping than category.

Description: Free-text search keywords / typical procurement terms associated with the standard.
Notes: Feeds directly into embedding_text; keep concise and specific.

Description: BIS technical department/sectional committee responsible for the standard.
Example: Cement and Concrete Sectional Committee, CED 2
Always Available?: No — confirmed for about half the collected standards
Notes: Useful for provenance, not for search/embeddings.

Description: Current revision label and reaffirmation/withdrawal status.
Always Available?: No — several standards show 'Not available on reviewed BIS page'
Notes: IMPORTANT: standards get revised/withdrawn. This field needs periodic refresh, not a one-time snapshot. NOTE (added on review): In File 07 (Master Dataset), this field is split into two columns — 'status' and 'revision_information' — rather than one combined field. Same concept, different shape; map both when writing code against File 07.

Description: Year (and where known, month) of the current edition.
Notes: Store as text (e.g. '2000') to avoid Excel date-parsing issues.

Description: Number and nature of amendments issued after the base edition.
Notes: Low priority for MVP; matters for compliance-grade accuracy later.

Description: Direct link to the official BIS page/document used as the source for this row.
Source: n/a — this IS the source pointer
Notes: Always link out to BIS rather than reproducing standard text in the UI.

Description: Type/name of the source page (catalogue page, product manual, circular, etc.).
Example: Official BIS 'Know Your Standard' catalogue page
Notes: Helps the team judge reliability — a full standard PDF is stronger evidence than a circular table row. NOTE (added on review): In File 07 (Master Dataset), this is just called 'source' (matches this row exactly). In File 02 it was originally mislabeled 'source_page' — that has been corrected to 'source' so both files now agree.

Description: Other IS numbers this standard references or is referenced by.
Notes: Could later power a 'related standards' feature.

Description: Formal list of other standards normatively referenced (stricter subset of related_standard_information).
Always Available?: No — not systematically collected in this pass
Notes: Not collected for this handoff; flagged for future work.

Description: Notes on associated test methods / BIS test-report volumes.
Example: 16713 BIS test reports issued (high certification volume)
Always Available?: Partial (only for standards from that circular)
Notes: Indicates how actively a standard is certified against — a rough popularity signal.

Description: Whether BIS certification (ISI mark) is mandatory, voluntary, or not applicable for this standard.
Notes: Helps distinguish 'must comply' standards from voluntary/reference codes in search results.

Description: Honest note on what could/could not be confirmed for this row.
Notes: Never hide gaps. If a field says 'Not available on reviewed BIS page', that is the correct, non-invented value. NOTE (added on review): In File 07 (Master Dataset), data_availability_notes and copyright_use_notes are both folded into a single 'notes' column rather than kept as two separate columns.

Description: Standard boilerplate note on IP status — see File 03 for full policy.
Example: Copyright vests in BIS; do not reproduce/redistribute full text without BIS permission
Notes: Same text repeats for every row by design — it is a policy reminder, not per-standard data.

Description: Concatenated clean text fed to the embedding model (see File 07).
Source: Derived — built from other fields, not a BIS field itself
Notes: See File 07 for the exact construction template.

Description: Structured JSON bundling secondary metadata fields for flexible querying.
Notes: Optional convenience field for the backend team (Muhaimin) — not required for the AI engine itself.
